Selection: [selection] mutually exclusive with [[trials]]; scope=full rejects on any unmet requirement (no silent shrink); subset freezes explicit ids + reason; repetitions default 1 with task+repetition groups. Bounds: concurrency default 1 enforced by real bounded execution; max_trials below derived count rejects; agent/verifier timeouts combine by narrowing; max_output_tokens enforceable only via pinned model-control equality; max_total_tokens/max_cost have no enforceable route this slice so declaring them rejects explicitly naming the gap (that rejection is the enforceability statement). run --plan re-verifies plan digest + material + experiment identity and executes exactly plan.trials; run --config C expands selection through the same resolve/freeze path; stage/settlement progress to stderr; saved report gains plan identity.

P19-D05 selection slice delivered. New `plan --config C [--native-material M|--fixtures F] --out P`: enumerates the pinned corpus inventory from task.toml metadata only (task packages generalize to corpus directories of task subdirectories; the single-task layout and every producer-pinned digest stay unchanged), expands the document's [selection] (scope=full|subset, explicit task_ids, recorded reason, repetitions, optional per-task seeds; mutually exclusive with [[trials]], ambiguity rejects) into exact deterministic trials (trial-<subject>-<task>-r<rep>, group <task>-r<rep>), and classifies every task's declared [environment] requirements against the local observations. Selected unmet/unknown requirements reject the whole request naming task+requirement+observation; scope=full rejects on any unmet corpus task (no silent shrink); the preview keeps per-task statuses for the whole inventory plus subjects/connection/trial count/concurrency/bounds. Bounds are explicit: concurrency defaults 1 and is enforced as an upper bound (hermetic trials execute in parallel waves of independent per-trial runtimes; native stays serial, bound never exceeded), max_trials rejects smaller expansions, agent/verifier timeouts combine by narrowing with the existing per-process limit and are frozen as the narrowed value, max_output_tokens is admitted only as the equal pinned model-control value (controls stay authoritative), and max_total_tokens/max_cost reject naming their missing enforcement route (that rejection is the enforceability statement). The frozen opi-eval-run-plan/1 file is digest-bound over the embedded experiment source, material identity (path + manifest byte digest), corpus entries, preflight, and exact trials. New `run --plan P --root R` re-verifies the plan digest, material bytes, experiment manifest identity, and re-expands the selection requiring exact-trial equality before executing; stage/settlement progress emits to stderr (execution line with width, per-trial stage=start and settled=sealed|failed); the saved run report gains the plan digest, selection projection, and execution width. `run --config C` remains the same resolve/freeze path ([selection] documents expand in run_experiment through the identical expansion). Task packages: loader + native/hermetic staging resolve per-task source directories from corpus roots; hermetic corpus fixtures carry per-task pinned profiles under profile/corpus/<task>.toml (byte-table + canonical package digest recomputed per task). A single-subject experiment (pi-only or opi-only) no longer needs an artificial comparison edge (resolve admits zero edges for exactly one subject; solo trials bind a solo:<subject> pair seed; single-subject reports carry empty pairs and complete). Latent deficits fixed: the material loader required instruction.md at the package root (blocked corpora), MissingEdges forced fabricated edges for single-subject documents, and owning_edge hard-required an edge for every trial. Recorded ceiling: native multi-task selection beyond the profile-bound task rejects explicitly (per-task production profiles are not materialized yet; deterministic multi-task execution is proven on the hermetic corpus fixture) - revisit when producers materialize per-task profiles.
